title: An Efficient RISC-V Vector Coprocessor for Heart Rate Variability Detection on Edge
problem: Continuous HRV (Heart Rate Variability) monitoring on edge/wearable devices is challenging due to lack of power and area-efficient processing optimized for this specific task.
motivation: Modern wearables need efficient, low-power continuous health monitoring. General-purpose processors are not optimized for HRV detection in terms of power and area efficiency.
method: Design of vector coprocessor based on open-source RISC-V ISA that offloads vector operations from main processor. Implements vector-aware HRV algorithm optimized for edge computing with chunked data processing for limited memory constraints.
key_novelty: Vector coprocessor design for RISC-V targeting HRV workload; vector-aware algorithm optimization for edge memory constraints.
contributions: RISC-V vector coprocessor for efficient HRV detection
Vector-aware HRV algorithm optimized for edge computing
Memory-efficient chunked data processing for limited edge device resources
80% power density improvement vs Ibex processor
limitations: Abstract only; no power consumption values, area overhead, or performance metrics provided; no comparison with other HRV accelerators.
primary_theme: Low-power specialized hardware for edge health monitoring
